edit.description: the entrypoint's stated reason for chaining rather than awaiting

summary: The budget hook's entrypoint justifies chaining on a loader claim measured false — a module the chain graph reaches may carry a top-level await

per.section: Narration is the ladder's bottom rung

acceptance: no site states that a module the chain loader reaches cannot carry a top-level await; the entrypoint either names a reason that reads true against the loader or names none
notes: Measured at this drain, twice: a `.flume/chain.ts` importing a module whose top level awaits loads clean through `loadChainModule` (the throw that follows is a hand-built paths object), and `tsImport` compiles a named-export and a default-only module carrying one as ESM and evaluates it. So the CJS-interop reason the comment states does not hold. The chained shape is not at issue — only its stated reason. Per note THE-ADAPTER-REGISTERS-THE-BUDGET-HOOK, whose platform-fact candidate this is.
